newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African shares end weaker ahead of long-weekend.
newsitem.headline: S.African shares end weaker ahead of long-weekend.

text.p: South African shares ended flat in Friday's listless trade, but a swathe of overnight foreign assets swaps boostd volumes as Gencor closed with 4.1 million shares traded on the counter, dealers said.

Gencor ended down 80 cents at 19.75 rand following a large corporate finance deal on the stock involving some 3.2 million shares valued at around 67 million rand earlier, dealers said. They said some reluctance by market players to take positions ahead of the June futures close-out next week hurt the industrials which were also weighed down by profit-taking.
Industrials ended down 19.7 points at 8,482.4, golds were off 19.1 points at 1,129.0 and the all-share index closed down 21.2 points at 7,271.5.
Dealers said bullion's hold below the pshycologically-important $350 an ounce level continued to cripple golds.

They said while precious metal stocks were in gloom, the finance and banking sectors continued to tread on positive ground with continuing hopes that Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals might cut interest rates later this year.
The financial index hit another fresh high on Friday when it added 21.9 points to 9,805.9.
Dealers said despite a lethargic trade session volumes ended strong with around 860 million rand worth of shares traded by close compared to 901 million rand worth of shares on Thursday.
In the broader market the declines led advances by 220 to 152, while 31 shares hit new highs and 27 dropped to new lows.
Johannesburg Stock Exchange officials said an all time weekly high of 52,138 deals or trades had been reached on Friday.
The previous high of 50,197 was recorded in the week ended 16 May, they added.
The bourse will be closed on Monday, June 16, for Youth Day holiday.
